_disclaimer: SIMULATED DEMONSTRATION VALUES -- NOT CLINICAL GUIDELINES. These weights express how much each kind of missing or conflicting information should reduce our stated confidence in a prototype. They are not calibrated against outcome data and carry no clinical authority.
_what_confidence_means: Confidence is a statement about the INPUT DATA, not about the patient. 40% confidence does not mean the patient is probably fine. It means we are working with a thin, stale or contradictory picture and a human should look sooner, not later. Confidence never changes the risk score.
_four_drivers: Confidence starts at 1.0 and is reduced by four named, independently testable drivers. Each one reports its own quality figure and its own plain-English reasons, so the nurse sees WHY we are unsure, not just THAT we are.
_completeness_note: How much of the expected picture we actually hold. Sub-weights sum to 1.0 within this driver.
_baseline_note: Do we know what NORMAL looks like for this specific patient? Multiplicative penalties: a patient with an undocumented face AND no record on file is worse off than either alone. The facial penalty is the largest single number in this file, on purpose -- it is the P016 case.
_provenance_note: Phase 6 added WHERE a baseline came from, not just whether one exists. weak_provenance_max_penalty scales with the reliability figures in data/facial_config.json: a baseline the patient recalled themselves costs more confidence than one documented across three prior visits. It costs CONFIDENCE only. A weakly-sourced baseline never adds points, because escalating on weak provenance would fall hardest on patients least likely to have records.
_agreement_note: Do the modalities tell the same story? Each modality returns concerning / reassuring / silent. Silence is not agreement, so it neither helps nor hurts here -- it is already charged to completeness.
_staleness_note: A 90-minute-old SpO2 is weaker evidence than one taken two minutes ago. This driver is what makes re-triage (Phase 10) meaningful: a patient who is not re-measured LOSES confidence as they wait, which is the correct behaviour for the silent-deterioration failure mode.
_plausible_bands_note: The uncertainty interval is ASYMMETRIC on purpose. Missing information can conceal danger; it cannot manufacture safety. The upward span is the full 100-point range because at zero confidence we cannot honestly exclude any band, and the downward reach is a quarter of it, representing measurement noise only. At full confidence the interval collapses onto the score. This is a monotone widening rule, NOT a calibrated conformal predictor -- see the README for what we do and do not claim.
_review_note: Consumed by Phase 7. Low confidence is not itself an escalation; low confidence ALONGSIDE a concerning finding is.
